## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

8	// into every consuming repo, so it must never carry deployment detail or anything
9	// adjacent to a credential: `invocation_endpoint: 'fleet'` names a key, and the
10	// repo's own config maps that key to a URL and to the NAME of the repo Actions
11	// secret holding its token. That indirection is also what replaces the whole
12	// self/fleet apparatus — reach is a property of which endpoint you call, so a
13	// task needing wider access names a different endpoint and nothing else in the
14	// system needs a concept of scope.

2	// iteration: pick the next ready item, claim it by a verified lease, evaluate the
3	// precondition (THE only place it is ever evaluated), then on a go run prework and
4	// either converge (agentless) or hand off to an agent session; on a no-go roll a
5	// scheduled item to its next anchor with the reason on record.

7	// An executor's whole interface is issue read/write plus the repo at HEAD, which
8	// is what makes it platform-agnostic: the reference deployment is a job in the
9	// vendored workflows (the tick's post-tick drain, and a `labeled`-event run for
10	// latency), but a runner anywhere with an issues-scope token qualifies. Nothing
11	// enumerates executors; identity is self-declared in the claim comment.

37	// rules read live at pick time.

39	//  - SAME-TITLE MUTEX (S15/F6): skip an item whose exact title has another open
40	//    item executing or handed to an agent — one task, one execution at a time,

43	//    [T]` while T's standing item is live THIS CYCLE (ready / executing / agent).
44	//    A rolled upstream (blocked until its next anchor: it declined this cycle)

59	    .filter((i) => !open.some((o) => o.number !== i.number && titleOf(o) === titleOf(i)
60	      && (hasLabel(o, EXECUTING) || hasLabel(o, AGENT))))
61	    .filter((i) => {
62	      if (!hasLabel(i, ORIGIN_SCHEDULE)) return true;
63	      return !taskAfter(taskIdOf(i)).some(liveUpstream);
64	    })
65	    .sort((a, b) =>
66	      (hasLabel(b, URGENT) ? 1 : 0) - (hasLabel(a, URGENT) ? 1 : 0)
67	      || new Date(a.created_at) - new Date(b.created_at)
68	      || a.number - b.number);
69	}

72	// because executor identity is an unbounded set and must never become a label
73	// (DESIGN §4).

# instantiate each task's standing item at its anchor, ready what is due, reclaim
# dead executor claims — and evaluates no precondition and collects no signal. The
# drain is an ordinary executor run: it picks up what the tick just created, which
# is what keeps the common case's latency at zero even with no `labeled` event
# delivered. Lost events are therefore never the only delivery — they are latency
# sugar, which is what retires the re-arm.

# lever every forced run, migration and validation burst depends on.

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '49 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

# One tick at a time, always. The tick's duplicate-standing-item self-heal is
# written assuming exactly this — it closes every open family item but the oldest,
# which is safe precisely because two ticks never run at once.
concurrency:
  group: claudinite-tick
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write        # read the repo + vendored engine; a task's prework pushes its delivery branch
  issues: write          # create / label / comment / close work items — the queue itself

  actions: write         # dispatch a workflow a task drives (creating a workflow_dispatch event needs write; `read` silently 403s the POST)

jobs:

    steps:

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5

      - name: Instantiate, ready and reclaim work items
        env:

        run: node .claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/queue/tick.mjs

  # leash (60m): a hung runner has to be killed by the platform before its claim
  # is reaped and the item re-picked, or a zombie's prework runs beside its
  # replacement's.
  drain:
    needs: tick
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 50
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5

      - name: Drain the queue

  # issue by a fixed title (create-or-comment), and ensures the label first since a

name: Claudinite scheduler

on:

    inputs:
      wake:

# written assuming exactly this — it closes every open family item but the oldest,

concurrency:

  cancel-in-progress: false

  issues: write          # create / label / comment / close work items — the queue itself
  pull-requests: write   # a task's prework opens its PR and arms auto-merge

  # is reaped and the item re-picked, or a zombie's prework runs beside its

          # configured invocation endpoint's token, below this marker — by name.
          # claudinite:secrets

  # failure to a human-visible `workflow-failure` issue. Converges to ONE open
  # issue by a fixed title (create-or-comment), and ensures the label first since a
  # first-run failure may precede any label-ensure.

    needs: [tick, drain]
    if: failure()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      issues: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/github-script@v7

          script: |
            const { owner, repo } = context.repo;
            const title = 'Claudinite scheduler run failed';
            await github.rest.issues.createLabel({ owner, repo, name: 'workflow-failure', color: 'b60205', description: 'Claudinite scheduler: a scheduler run or task failed' }).catch(() => {});

            const body = `The Claudinite tick/drain run failed: ${run}`;
            const found = await github.rest.search.issuesAndPullRequests({ q: `repo:${owner}/${repo} is:issue is:open in:title "${title}"` });

name: UI requirements

# The executable-requirements UI lane: renders the real pages in the pinned
# headless Chromium and compares pixel-exact against the committed goldens
# (product/requirements/). Deliberately NOT part of the static-website pack's
# vendored `static-site-ci.yml` — that file belongs to the pack and is
# overwritten on every re-vendor, and this lane is this repo's own. The fast
# gate (`scripts/verify.sh`, which includes the requirements coverage and
# gallery checks) runs there as the declared `test_command`; only the browser
# work lives here, so the fast lane stays browser-free.
#
# The Playwright version installed here must match the harness's pin
# (product/requirements/shared/harness/browser.js) or the run refuses to
# compare. workflow_dispatch so a run can be started by hand on a branch whose
# pull_request event never fired.

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ui-requirements-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  ui-requirements:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "22"
      - name: Install pinned Playwright + Chromium
        run: |
          npm i --no-save playwright@1.56.1
          npx playwright install --with-deps chromium
      - name: UI requirements (screen + behavior)
        run: npm run test:ui
      - name: Upload failure artifacts (actual/diff renders)
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: requirements-failure-artifacts
          path: product/requirements/shared/.artifacts/
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          # The artifacts dir is dot-prefixed, and this action skips hidden
          # paths by default — without this the diffs silently never upload,
          # which is exactly when they are needed.
          include-hidden-files: true
